slides.3.title: Geography and Climate of Trás-os-Montes
slides.3.html:
Trás-os-Montes (literally "behind the mountains") lies in the northeast corner of Portugal next to Spain, cut off from the coast by the Marão and Alvão mountains.

🌡️ Extreme continental climate

  • Portugal's most extreme continental climate: "nine months of winter, three months of hell"
  • Summer highs of over 40°C and winter lows of -10°C
  • Low annual rainfall (400–700mm), mostly in winter
  • Day-night temperature swings of 20–25°C help the grapes retain acidity

🪨 Soils

  • Mainly granite (north) and schist (south and the Valpaços area)
  • Poor soils give low yields from the vines but concentrated fruit

🗺️ Three sub-regions

  • Chaves: the northernmost, close to Spain, with a slight Atlantic influence
  • Valpaços: central, with the most typical continental climate
  • Planalto Mirandês: the easternmost, a plateau with a farming mix of grapes, olives and almonds
slides.4.title: The Three DOC Sub-regions of Trás-os-Montes
slides.4.items.0.desc: The northernmost, closest to Spain's Galicia; whites (Gouveio) are fresher and reds are fruity
slides.4.items.1.desc: Central plateau, the most typical continental climate. Touriga Nacional and Tinta Amarela perform well
slides.4.items.2.desc: Eastern plateau near Spain. Fernão Pires and Trincadeira are interplanted; Portugal's most remote DOC
slides.5.question: What is the literal meaning of "Trás-os-Montes" in Portuguese?
slides.5.explanation: Trás-os-Montes means "behind the mountains" in Portuguese, because the region is cut off from the western coast by the Marão and Alvão mountains. This geographic isolation creates Portugal's most extreme continental climate: hot summers, cold winters and a very large annual temperature range.
slides.6.question: What is the climate of Trás-os-Montes?
slides.6.options.2: Extreme continental, hot summers, cold winters, large temperature range
slides.6.explanation: Trás-os-Montes has Portugal's most extreme continental climate, with summers above 40°C and winters down to -10°C, described as "nine months of winter, three months of hell". These extremes allow the grapes to ripen fully while retaining relatively high natural acidity.
